# xfo-miner v1.0.13

This release adds an operator-requested GPU diagnostic response path so the pool can request bounded hardware/runtime evidence from a connected miner during support investigations.

## Highlights

- Adds `gpu_diagnostic_request` handling from Pool to Miner.
- Sends `gpu_diagnostic_report` replies with miner version, host OS/arch, safe capability summaries, startup GPU inventory, fresh GPU scan output, and bounded command evidence.
- Keeps diagnostics local and bounded: command output is truncated, NUL bytes are stripped, and existing safe capability fields are reused.

## Scope

### GPU diagnostic handoff

- `internal/pool/protocol.go` defines the diagnostic request/report message contract.
- `internal/pool/client.go` supports enqueueing diagnostic reports over the existing WebSocket client.
- `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go` routes `gpu_diagnostic_request` messages to the diagnostic builder.
- `internal/scheduler/gpu_diagnostic.go` collects safe runtime evidence from `nvidia-smi`, `clinfo`, and Hashcat inspection commands when available.

## Validation

- Release validation:
  - `git --no-pager diff --check -- cmd/xfo-miner/main.go internal/pool/client.go internal/pool/protocol.go internal/scheduler/gpu_diagnostic.go internal/scheduler/scheduler.go internal/scheduler/scheduler_test.go internal/telemetry/reporter_test.go .github/releases/v1.0.13.md`
  - `miner-ci` on push runs `go test ./...` and cross-builds Linux amd64/arm64, Windows amd64, and macOS amd64/arm64.
  - `miner-release` on tag builds deterministic release packages, uploads `latest.json`, validates the public release surface, and publishes GitHub release assets.

## Operator notes

- Use v1.0.13 when debugging miner-side GPU visibility, OpenCL/Hashcat detection, or startup GPU inventory mismatches.
- Diagnostic command failures are reported inside the payload instead of crashing the miner.
- Forced OTA remains disabled in `--debug` mode, matching previous miner safety semantics.
